عَطَوَّدٌ Hard, severe, rigorous, or difficult: (IDrd, O, L, K:) applied in this sense to anything: and particularly to a journey: or in this case meaning distant. (L.) ―
-b2- A quick pace, or rate of going: (S, O, L, K:) and so عَطَرَّدٌ [q. v.]. (L.) ―
-b3- A high mountain: (O, L, K, TA: [in the CK, من الحِبالِ is erroneously put for مِنَ الجِبَالِ:]) as also عَصَوَّدٌ and عَطَرَّدٌ. (L.) ―
-b4- A long day: (O, K:) a complete day (L) or year: (Ibn-'Abbád, O, K:) a whole day. (T, O, L, K.) One says, ذَهَبَ عَطَوَّدًا He went away a whole day. (O, K.) ―
-b5- A conspicuous, clear, open, road, along which one goes whithersoever he will. (ISh, O, L, K.) ―
-b6- A generous, noble, liberal, man. (Ibn-'Abbád, O, K.) ―
-b7- A sharpened spearhead. (Ibn-'Abbád, O, K.) ―
-b8- Accord. to [IDrd and] Az [and J], this word is quasi-coordinate to the quinqueliteral-radical class. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
